name: GET /api/vault/keys/:key_id — read one key within the tenant — sdk-vault

testCases.name: Read a key the calling tenant owns
A key id that does not exist is not found

description: Reads ONE vault key, and only if it belongs to the calling tenant. Returns the same metadata-only projection as the list route — no key material exists in vault.key to return. The tenant predicate is part of the SQL (getKeyForTenant), so the ownership check cannot be skipped by a caller that forgets it. A key belonging to ANOTHER tenant answers 404, never 403: a 403 would confirm that the id EXISTS somewhere, which is precisely the fact a caller enumerating ids is trying to learn, so absence and denial are made indistinguishable from outside. Edge cases: a non-existent id and another tenant's id are deliberately the same 404 with the same body; a key at root/app/pool tier is also 404 to a tenant token because those rows carry tenant_id NULL; a shredded key still reads back, showing state 'shredded' with shredded_at set and kms_ref NULL, because the row is the audit trail of the erasure and must remain readable; a malformed (non-UUID) key_id is a 500 from the uuid cast rather than a 400, which is worth tightening but is recorded here as the current behaviour.

errorCases.when: No Authorization header, or not in Bearer form — rejected by the gateway default-deny authGate before requireAuth

errorCases.message: This token carries no tenant, so no key scope can be derived
errorCases.when: The JWT verifies but carries no tenant_id claim
No key with that id within the calling tenant — covers both a genuinely unknown id and a key owned by another tenant, deliberately indistinguishable
key_id is not a valid UUID so the ::uuid cast raises 22P02, or the database is unavailable
